history.summary: A 48-unit freehold shoebox/serviced-apartment block in Geylang with only 14 URA transactions — the high headline appreciation (6.8%) rests on too thin a sample to trust, and the development is small, niche and carries Geylang stigma. Despite a high MMR, the exit-liquidity case is weak for an investment hold.
history.rating_rationale: 721sqft 2BR at $1.10M / $1,526 psf is ~20% below the project median PSF ($1,896) on paper, but with just 14 URA transactions the 6.8% CAGR is statistically unreliable and the 48-unit block offers thin, slow liquidity. Freehold and decent 5%+ rental yield (Aljunied/Paya Lebar tenant demand) are real positives, but Geylang-fringe stigma narrows the resale buyer pool. MMR 1563 / score 863 overstates the case given the data thinness.

history.summary: The algo's -19.5% cohort discount rests on ZERO cohort transactions and only 14 appreciation txns, so the 'value' signal is unreliable; the asking PSF is mid-range at best, on a tiny 48-unit illiquid Geylang freehold block where location and liquidity are the real risks.
history.rating_rationale: Asking $1,526 PSF (721 sqft, $1.1M). The dossier shows psf_cohort_txns=0, so the -19.5% cohort premium is a pure data quirk with no comparable behind it; appreciation rests on only 14 txns (6.79% CAGR, which v3.4 priors discount to ~0 forward power). Verified project pricing: last-12-mo avg ~$1,630 PSF, range $1,261-$1,741, with a comparable 753 sqft 2BR listed at $1,448 PSF. So the asking is below the 12-mo average but above the cheapest current comp — mid-range, not a clear bargain. Structural drags dominate: a single-block 48-unit project (Macly, small developer) with only ~8 transactions in 3 years = very low liquidity and wide spreads, plus Geylang sub-locale that can constrain financing and resale demand. Freehold is not a forward edge. Without a verified discount or catalyst, this is a thin-data, illiquid hold.
